1	### Workflow
2	
3	**Mandatory ordering — methodology before evidence.** Follow [SKILL.md](SKILL.md)'s standard workflow strictly in sequence. Load all applicable instructions before investigation or action. The bounded routing exception below selects instructions only; it permits no behavioral analysis, findings, full-diff investigation, edits or tests.
4	
5	Copy and complete this checklist:
6	
7	```
8	Code Review Progress:
9	- [ ] Step 1: Load basic instructions
10	- [ ] Step 2: Resolve scope from filenames/metadata
11	- [ ] Step 3: Detect profiles and route all checklists
12	- [ ] Step 4: Read every resolved checklist
13	- [ ] Step 5: Investigate behavior and compatibility
14	- [ ] Step 6: Apply profile and general checklists
15	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check and confidence assessment
16	- [ ] Step 8: Index findings
17	- [ ] Step 9: Present findings, coverage and verdict
18	- [ ] Step 10: Confirm next steps
19	- [ ] Step 11: Verify outputs
20	```
21	
22	### 1) Load basic instructions
23	
24	Read this entire process and [shared-capy-knowledge-protocol.md](shared-capy-knowledge-protocol.md), [shared-profile-detection.md](shared-profile-detection.md), [shared-review-scope-protocol.md](shared-review-scope-protocol.md), [shared-change-context.md](shared-change-context.md), and [functional-review.md](functional-review.md) before routing. Already loaded, unchanged instructions need not be read twice. The common context and functional method apply even without active profiles or specification documents.
25	
26	### 2) Resolve scope from filenames/metadata
27	
28	Use `git status -sb` and diff statistics/filenames only. Honor an explicit user-selected scope/range; otherwise select unstaged changes, falling back to staged changes when none are unstaged. If neither exists, report no changes and request a range. Record the chosen selector and keep it for investigation. Do not silently combine staged and unstaged scopes.
29	
30	A large diff (>500 lines) needs focused batching, not an early content dump. A feature-directory listing may locate task documents; their detailed reading belongs to investigation.
31	
32	### 3) Detect profiles and route all checklists
33	
34	Invoke [shared-profile-detection.md](shared-profile-detection.md) with the scoped filenames. Read each known profile's `DETECTION.md` and evaluate its authoritative signals; do not stop enumerating after an obvious extension match. Path matches alone do not activate a profile. Multiple profiles may apply. Resolve the plugin root from this skill's loaded location (parent of `skills/`) and construct absolute profile paths; do not forward unresolved root tokens into tools.
35	
36	Batch the Known-profile reads together when supported, then reconcile expected paths with completed lookups. Record each rule's match/non-match or the shared procedure's explicit unavailable-file outcome; apply that procedure's ENOENT and root-resolution fallbacks. A skipped lookup leaves routing incomplete even when a file extension suggests an obvious profile. This prevents an assumed negative from hiding an additional applicable profile.
37	
38	For every active profile, read its `profiles/<profile>/review-code/index.md`. Collect **Always load** entries. Evaluate filename/metadata **Load if:** predicates first. For declared content predicates in detection or conditional loading, inspect at most approximately 16 KiB per candidate file, solely to resolve the predicate; log predicate/path. Apply the detection protocol's YAML document rules where relevant. If a conditional cannot be decided within the bound, conservatively select its instruction. Do not defer any conditional until after full source investigation.
39	
40	Collect `(profile, checklist, triggered_by)` records for all matching/conservatively selected entries, carrying detection provenance and noting conservative selections. Indexes are authoritative; never hardcode checklist names. No profile means an empty list, not omission of the common method.
41	
42	### 4) Read every resolved checklist
43	
44	Read each selected `profiles/<profile>/review-code/<checklist>` using the resolved absolute plugin root. An index read is routing, not checklist loading: every selected link requires its own returned file content, even for a tiny diff. Keep the resolved paths as a loading ledger and mark them loaded only when their read results arrive. Do not batch investigation commands with these reads.
45	
46	Before proceeding, emit a compact loading checkpoint naming the completed common-instruction reads, every known profile's detection-lookup outcome, and the loaded checklist paths (or explicitly no active profiles). Any selected path without returned content keeps the gate closed; surface unreadable instructions and stop, except for detection fallbacks explicitly defined by the shared procedure. This checkpoint records evidence already obtained, not a promise to load guidance later. It catches accidental index-to-diff shortcuts without creating a separate artifact or replacing the actual read events.
47	
48	### 5) Investigate behavior and compatibility
49	
50	This is the single entry point for subject-matter investigation. With methodology loaded:
51	
52	- Read the full diff using the selector from scope and re-read every changed file at the reviewed revision, accounting for deletions. Do not rely on an earlier conversation's contents. Use index blobs for staged review and the selected candidate revision for a commit range; do not silently substitute unrelated worktree contents.
53	- Read relevant requirements and task documents; build task scope with the shared protocol. Establish the shared change context, distinguishing review base/candidate from any release baseline.
54	- Apply the common functional method: trace changed behavior through relevant dependencies and unchanged consumers, exercise concrete scenarios, and assess relevant delivery combinations. Obtain actual historical source when needed; label provenance and unavailable evidence using the shared context rules.
55	- Search `kk:review-findings` for relevant patterns and, for active programming-language profiles, `kk:lang-idioms`. With no language results, optionally index a canonical idioms source under that label. Skip language lookup for non-language profiles.
56	
57	If investigation adds targets covered by new profiles or newly applicable conditionals, pause analysis of those targets and return to routing/loading before continuing. Subsequent focused re-reads, reproductions and verification substantiate findings within this investigation; they do not create another full-diff preflight. Keep claims within actual access and evidence.
58	
59	### 6) Apply profile and general checklists
60	
61	Apply every loaded `(profile, checklist, triggered_by)` record to the affected behavior and diff. Domain checklists supplement the common method. Tag findings with their profile/checklist origin and detection signal; use `Profile: generic · Checklist: —` and `Triggered by: —` for common reasoning. Keep severity-major output and merge duplicate issues across lenses.
62	
63	General guidance that applies regardless of profile — apply these categories on every diff, whether or not a profile-specific checklist covered them:
64	
65	- **SOLID / architecture:** SRP violations (overloaded modules with unrelated responsibilities), OCP (frequent edits to add behavior instead of extension points), LSP (subclasses that break expectations or require type checks), ISP (wide interfaces with unused methods), DIP (high-level logic tied to low-level implementations). When you propose a refactor, explain _why_ it improves cohesion/coupling and outline a minimal, safe split. If refactor is non-trivial, propose an incremental plan instead of a large rewrite.
66	- **Security / reliability:** XSS, injection (SQL/NoSQL/command), SSRF, path traversal; AuthZ/AuthN gaps, missing tenancy checks; secret leakage or API keys in logs/env/files; rate limits, unbounded loops, CPU/memory hotspots; unsafe deserialization, weak crypto, insecure defaults; race conditions, check-then-act, TOCTOU, missing locks. Call out both **exploitability** and **impact**.
67	- **Code quality:** error handling (swallowed exceptions, overly broad catch, missing handling, async errors); performance (N+1 queries, CPU-intensive ops in hot paths, missing cache, unbounded memory); boundary conditions (null/undefined, empty collections, numeric boundaries, off-by-one). Flag issues that may cause silent failures or production incidents.
68	- **Removal candidates:** unused, redundant, or feature-flagged-off code. Distinguish **safe delete now** vs **defer with plan**; provide concrete follow-up steps with checkpoints (tests/metrics).
69	
70	### 7) Self-check and confidence assessment
71	
72	For **each finding** from Steps 5–6:
73	
74	1. Re-read the relevant code and surrounding context independently.
75	2. Ask: **"Could I be misreading the code?"** — trace execution paths, check for runtime behavior, configuration, or framework conventions that might make this correct.
76	3. Ask: **"Is this a real issue or a style preference?"** — distinguish between bugs/risks and subjective choices that don't affect correctness or security.
77	4. Ask: **"What's the actual impact?"** — verify that the severity matches the real-world consequence, not just the theoretical violation.
78	5. Assign final confidence score (1–100%) with **explicit reasoning** documenting:
79	   - What was verified
80	   - What evidence supports the finding
81	   - What uncertainty remains
82	6. Downgrade or **remove** findings that don't survive the self-check.
83	
84	### 8) Index findings
85	
86	Index any P0/P1 findings that suggest a systemic or structural pattern (not isolated typos or one-off mistakes) as `kk:review-findings`. Index on first encounter — recurrence detection happens on the search side in future reviews.
87	
88	- If no P0/P1 systemic findings exist, explicitly note "No findings to index" and move on.
89	- This step is mandatory — do not skip it even if the review found no issues.
90	
91	### 9) Present results
92	
93	#### Output format
94	
95	Structure your review as follows:
96	
97	```markdown
98	## Code Review Summary
99	
100	**Files reviewed**: X files, Y lines changed
101	**Overall assessment**: [APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / COMMENT]
102	**Intent and scope**: requirement source, current task/request, selected diff and candidate state
103	**Baselines**: review base/candidate; separate release baseline if applicable
104	
105	## Behavior and Compatibility
106	
107	Inspected paths/scenarios, observed results and evidence limits. Include applicable
108	Supported / Blocked / Unknown / Not applicable conclusions with named baselines.
109	Attribute author-supplied results and inherited issues. Record outstanding evidence
110	or release prerequisites, next actions and durable tracking locations when deferred.
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Findings
115	
116	### P0 - Critical
117	
118	(none or list)
119	
120	### P1 - High
121	
122	- **[file:line]** Brief title
123	  - Profile: {profile_name} · Checklist: {checklist_filename}
124	  - Triggered by: {signal_type} — {signal_description}
125	  - Trigger/path, expected vs actual result and consequence
126	  - Confidence: 90% - reasoning behind the confidence level
127	  - Suggested fix
128	
129	- **[another_file:line]** Brief title
130	  - Profile: generic · Checklist: —
131	  - Triggered by: —
132	  - Trigger/path, expected vs actual result and consequence
133	  - Confidence: 60% - reasoning behind the confidence level
134	  - Suggested fix
135	
136	### P2 - Medium
137	
138	...
139	
140	### P3 - Low
141	
142	...
143	
144	---
145	
146	## Removal/Iteration Plan
147	
148	(if applicable)
149	
150	## Additional Suggestions
151	
152	(optional improvements, not blocking)
153	```
154	
155	**Inline comments**: Use this format for file-specific findings:
156	
157	```
158	::code-comment{file="path/to/file" line="42" severity="P1"}
159	Description of the issue and suggested fix.
160	::
161	```
162	
163	Apply [functional-review.md](functional-review.md)'s verdict mapping: a hard acceptance/delivery violation cannot be approved; material Unknown evidence receives COMMENT absent a demonstrated blocker. Out-of-scope operational unknowns do not automatically downgrade an explicitly scoped code verdict. Preserve P0–P3 impact severity and distinguish code correctness from release readiness.
164	
165	**Every review** reports coverage and limits, even with findings. When no issues are found, explicitly state:
166	
167	- What was checked
168	- Any areas not covered (e.g., "Did not verify database migrations")
169	- Residual risks or recommended follow-up tests
170	
171	### 10) Next steps confirmation
172	
173	After presenting findings, ask user how to proceed:
174	
175	```markdown
176	---
177	
178	## Next Steps
179	
180	I found X issues (P0: ..., P1: ..., P2: ..., P3: ...).
181	
182	The actionable items I recommend fixing:
183	1. P1 ...
184	2. P2 ...
185	3. P3 ...
186	
187	Items I recommend keeping as is:
188	- ...: the finding is a false-positive because ...
189	- ...: correct behavior because ...
190	- ...: mirrors production behavior of ...
191	
192	**How would you like to proceed?**
193	
194	1. **Fix all** - I'll implement all suggested fixes
195	2. **Fix P0/P1 only** - Address critical and high priority issues
196	3. **Fix specific items** - Tell me which issues to fix
197	4. **No changes** - Review complete, no implementation needed
198	
199	Please choose an option or provide specific instructions.
200	```
201	
202	**Important**: Do NOT implement any changes until user explicitly confirms. This is a review-first workflow.
203	
204	### 11) Verify outputs
205	
206	Before declaring the review complete, check each item in the **Required Outputs** section of SKILL.md:
207	
208	- [ ] Review report presented to user
209	- [ ] Intent, scope/baselines, inspected behavior, applicable compatibility conclusions and evidence limits reported
210	- [ ] P0/P1 systemic findings indexed as `kk:review-findings` (or explicitly noted "No findings to index")
211	- [ ] Next steps confirmation from user
212	
213	If any item is unchecked, go back and complete it before proceeding.
214
